text: Welcome to Chapter 6 — the capstone. Everything up to this point has been building toward one project: a real, working chat application, built against Anthropic's Messages API. Not a toy single request — a genuine multi-turn conversation loop, the same shape under the hood as every commercial chat product you've used.

Here's the shape of it. The app keeps a growing message history. Every turn, it sends that full history to Claude. The reply streams back token by token instead of appearing all at once. And the loop keeps going until the user chooses to end the conversation. Small project, real production pattern.

Chapter 1 explained why the model needs the full history every single time — it has no memory of its own between calls. Chapter 2 is why you'll pick a specific model deliberately, not by default. Chapter 3 is the build itself — chat completions, roles, and streaming are the exact three lessons this project assembles. And Chapter 4 is why you're not fine-tuning anything here — a good system prompt does this job instead.

Before Lesson 30, get your environment ready. Install the SDK with pip install anthropic. Get an API key from the Claude Console and set it as an environment variable — never hard-coded in your file. Then run a one-line sanity check: a single message call with a short max_tokens. If it prints a real reply back, you're ready to build.

Four things your finished build needs to do. Maintain a growing messages list across turns, not just one request and exit. Stream the reply so it prints incrementally. Include a system prompt that gives the assistant an actual persona or purpose. And let the user type something like "quit" to exit cleanly.

Environment ready, rubric clear, every prior chapter pointing at this one build. Next lesson is the walkthrough itself — the real, verified streaming code, piece by piece, until you have a working chat application.
